tagline: Bridges and causeways link island orchards with Vermont’s lakeside mainland
intro: Lake Champlain’s island drive links bridges and causeways before reaching the mainland at Milton and continuing south to Burlington. The formal Lake Champlain Byway runs 184 miles through Grand Isle, Chittenden and Addison counties. It is a Vermont-designated byway whose council highlights scenery, nature, recreation, history and culture. The greater Burlington section includes urban, suburban and rural communities.

Before the US highway number, the Alburgh-to-Burlington road belonged to Route 30 in the 1922 New England road-marking system. The northern crossing began with a ferry between Rouses Point and Alburgh. US 2 initially followed that ferry route; a tolled swing bridge carried the highway across in 1937. A permanent, toll-free bridge replaced the swing bridge in 1987. The Lake Champlain Byway Council formed in 2004 to coordinate promotion and preservation of the designated corridor.

Start on the Rouses Point Bridge and follow US 2 through Alburgh and North Hero toward Grand Isle and South Hero. US 2 is signed east even while the Alburgh-to-Burlington stretch carries you south. At South Hero, the causeway reaches Sand Bar State Park on the mainland. Beyond Burlington, US 7 leads through Shelburne and Charlotte toward Addison County, between the Adirondacks and Green Mountains.

moments.title: Isle La Motte
moments.text: Isle La Motte’s dark building stone began in a shallow tropical sea. The island preserves remnants of the Chazy Fossil Reef, formed 480 million years ago. The fossil reefs became a National Natural Landmark in 2009, and a twenty-acre nature reserve protects reef outcrops on the island. Quarried limestone contains calcite and fossils of marine creatures; its dark color led sellers to market it as black marble. Fossil snails can be seen at the abandoned quarries. The island’s public library and Methodist church are among the buildings where the stone remains visible.
moments.notice: The public library and Methodist church display the island’s dark limestone.

moments.title: South Hero
moments.text: Apple orchards and dairy farms remain mainstays of South Hero’s agriculture. Farms held across generations operate alongside newer sustainable and organic ventures. The town occupies the southern half of Grand Isle, also called South Hero Island, and includes Providence, Stave and other smaller islands in Lake Champlain. Its village center lies along US 2. The highway continues north into Grand Isle town and east across the sandbar bridge into Milton. Across the lake to the west lie Plattsburgh and Peru, New York; across its eastern arm lies Milton, on the Vermont mainland.

moments.title: Sand Bar State Park
moments.text: The US 2 causeway follows a natural sandbar between South Hero Island and the Vermont mainland. At its eastern end, Sand Bar State Park preserves a large stone bathhouse built by the Civilian Conservation Corps in 1933–35. CCC crews cleared, filled and graded what had been swampy marshland to develop the park. The bathhouse’s upper floor originally housed caretakers and lifeguards and now serves as storage; the rest continues in its original use. A stone grill built by the CCC also remains, beside a park whose facilities include a 2,000-foot sand beach.
moments.notice: The CCC-built stone bathhouse remains the park’s most prominent built feature.
